title: Radar/Spider Chart DI
tagline: Year 3 — Several variables on spokes around a centre: reading values, profiles and comparisons

introduction.overview: A radar (or spider) chart plots several variables on spokes that radiate from a centre, joining the points for each person or item into a polygon. Each spoke has its own scale starting at the centre. The chart is useful for comparing profiles: where one polygon sticks out beyond another, that item is stronger on that variable. In exams the polygon values are read from the rings; the questions are the same as for tables.
introduction.placementRelevance: Radar charts appear in DI sets as the "unusual" chart type to test flexibility.
introduction.realWorldContext: Skill profiles of candidates, product comparisons and performance reviews are often drawn as radar charts.

learningObjectives: Read values from spokes and rings
Compare two or more profiles variable by variable
Compute totals, averages and differences across spokes
Count where one profile leads another

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Each spoke is a separate scale starting at the centre. The value is read where the polygon crosses the spoke.

coreDefinitions: Spoke: one variable axis from the centre outwards.
Ring: a circle of equal value.
Profile: the polygon of one person or item.
Strength: a spoke where the profile reaches far out.
Lead: a variable on which one profile exceeds another.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A radar chart is a table wrapped in a circle. Unwrap it into a table and the questions are arithmetic.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write a table with one row per spoke and one column per profile. Then answer by looking up cells and doing simple arithmetic.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Difference
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Value A − value B on one spoke

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Lead count
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Number of spokes where A > B

mainNarrative: Write the table first: Communication 70, 80, 65; Logic 85, 75, 70; Technical 90, 70, 60; Teamwork 60, 85, 75; Leadership 55, 80, 90; Creativity 65, 72, 80 (Rahul, Sneha, Tarun).
Totals: Rahul 425, Sneha 462, Tarun 440. Averages: Rahul 70.8, Sneha 77.0, Tarun 73.3.
Strongest and weakest spokes: Rahul is strongest in Technical (90) and weakest in Leadership (55). Tarun is strongest in Leadership (90) and weakest in Technical (60).
Sneha leads Rahul on Communication, Teamwork, Leadership and Creativity: four spokes. Rahul leads on Logic and Technical.
Percent comparisons use the second named profile as the base: Sneha's Leadership (80) is (80 − 55) ÷ 55 = 45.5% higher than Rahul's.

deepDiveAspects.title: Area of the polygon
deepDiveAspects.content: A larger polygon suggests a stronger overall profile only if all spokes are on the same scale and equally important.

deepDiveAspects.title: Spoke order
deepDiveAspects.content: The order of spokes around the chart is arbitrary; do not read neighbours as related.

solvedExamples.title: Total
solvedExamples.question: Rahul scores 70, 85, 90, 60, 55 and 65 on six spokes. What is his total score?

solvedExamples.title: Lead count
solvedExamples.question: Compare Sneha (80, 75, 70, 85, 80, 72) with Rahul (70, 85, 90, 60, 55, 65). On how many spokes does Sneha lead?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Rahul leads on Logic and Technical.

solvedExamples.title: Percent more
solvedExamples.question: Sneha scores 80 in Leadership and Rahul 55. By what percentage is Sneha's score higher than Rahul's?

shortcutMethods.title: Unwrap the circle

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Read the chart for every question.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Copy the values into a table once and answer all questions from the table.

rulesForApplication: Use the second named profile as the base.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Follow the spoke to the ring.

placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Copy values into a table before answering.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Radar questions are table questions in disguise.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I compute a percentage with the right base?
